name: AI automation
title: AI Automation for Business Workflows in Pakistan
description: Work with Hamid to plan AI automation for enquiries, documents and routine operations, with clear approval steps, practical integrations and human oversight.
intro: AI automation combines software rules with AI to handle parts of a business process, such as organising enquiries or drafting a reply. I help businesses scope systems around their actual work, with clear limits on what the system can decide and when a person takes over.
problem: Repeated copying, sorting and follow-ups create a queue that grows with your business. The first step is identifying one recurring task, its inputs and the outcome your team needs. A predictable task may only need ordinary automation; AI becomes useful when the input includes varied language or documents.
audience: Small businesses and agencies handling repeated enquiries, internal document work or information moving between tools. Projects can be discussed remotely across Pakistan and internationally.
features: Enquiry categorisation with a review queue for ambiguous requests
Draft replies grounded in approved business information
Structured extraction from agreed document types
Logs, retry handling and notifications when a step fails
flow: Map a single process and identify decisions requiring approval.
Confirm the source data, tool access and permitted actions.
Build a small pilot and compare outputs against representative examples.
Review exceptions with your team before expanding the scope.
example: For example, a website enquiry could be checked for required fields, summarised for your team and assigned to the right person. A proposed reply can stay in draft until approved. This is an example scope, rather than a claim of a deployed client system.
integration: Potential connections include forms, email, spreadsheets, CRMs and AI APIs. Access, provider capabilities, usage costs and data handling are checked during discovery; integrations are selected for the task.

faqs.q: Does every automation need AI?
faqs.a: No. Fixed rules are often easier to test for predictable tasks. AI is considered when the process involves language, documents or inputs that vary.

faqs.q: How is accuracy checked?
faqs.a: Agree on representative test cases and acceptable outcomes before launch. Uncertain outputs should go to a person, and consequential actions should have explicit approval rules.

faqs.q: What determines the price?
faqs.a: Scope, integrations, data preparation, safeguards and ongoing provider usage. Share your current process for a scoped proposal; there is no fixed public package price.

descriptor: AI automation for repeatable business tasks

name: WhatsApp AI chatbot
title: WhatsApp AI Chatbot Development for Businesses
description: Plan a WhatsApp AI chatbot with Hamid for business FAQs, enquiry capture and human handover. Scope the knowledge, integrations and approval rules before launch.
intro: A WhatsApp AI chatbot helps customers ask questions through WhatsApp and receive answers from approved business information. I can scope a conversational system that collects useful enquiry details and hands the conversation to a person when needed.
problem: The same questions about services, hours and next steps can interrupt your team throughout the day. A chatbot needs more than a welcome message: it needs a reliable information source, boundaries for its replies and a clear way to reach a human.
audience: Service businesses and teams receiving repeat WhatsApp enquiries. It is most useful when someone owns the information and a team member can handle exceptions.
features: Answers using an approved FAQ or product information source
Step-by-step collection of enquiry details
Human handover with conversation context
Optional CRM or spreadsheet connection, subject to available APIs
flow: Review the business account, message requirements and provider options.
Organise approved answers and define escalation conditions.
Prototype customer journeys with realistic test conversations.
Verify permissions, handover and failure handling before launch.
example: A visitor might ask which service suits their need, share their contact details and request a callback. The chatbot can collect the information while reserving pricing exceptions or commitments for your team. Message availability and outbound behaviour depend on the approved platform setup.
integration: The official WhatsApp Business Platform or a suitable provider is assessed during discovery. Business verification, messaging requirements, language quality and usage charges must be confirmed for your account. Existing personal WhatsApp access alone does not establish API readiness.

faqs.q: Can it transfer a customer to a person?
faqs.a: Human handover can be included in the design. The receiving inbox, notification method and team responsibilities are agreed before implementation.

faqs.q: Can it answer in Urdu and English?
faqs.a: Language support can be evaluated with your approved content and sample conversations. It should be tested before being advertised as a supported feature.

faqs.q: Can it connect to a CRM?
faqs.a: Potentially, when the CRM provides suitable access. Field mapping, authentication, duplicates and consent requirements are checked first.

name: AI receptionist
title: AI Receptionist Planning and Development — Hamid
description: Scope an AI receptionist with Hamid to answer routine questions, collect callback requests and route enquiries, with clear human handover and booking rules.
intro: An AI receptionist is a conversational front desk that handles a defined set of enquiries and routes requests to your team. The right starting point is the reception work you want help with, rather than assuming every call or conversation can be automated.
problem: A missed enquiry and an incorrect booking can both create extra work. Reception automation must know the business hours, available services and when to stop. It should make no commitment beyond the information and permissions you approve.
audience: Appointment-based businesses and service teams needing a consistent first response. Text reception, appointment requests and voice reception are separate scopes, with channel feasibility assessed individually.
features: Approved answers about services and opening hours
Callback requests with contact and enquiry details
Routing to a relevant team member
Booking requests or confirmed bookings only with verified calendar access
flow: List the enquiries reception handles most often.
Choose a channel and confirm technical and account requirements.
Define booking, cancellation and escalation permissions.
Test ambiguous requests, unavailable times and human takeover.
example: For a consultation business, reception could explain the appointment process and collect preferred times. If the calendar cannot be checked reliably, the system should send a request for staff confirmation instead of claiming a booking is complete.
integration: Calendar, inbox and CRM connections depend on provider APIs and account access. Voice work also requires a separate assessment of telephony availability, language quality, recording arrangements and ongoing costs.

faqs.q: Is this a voice service or a chatbot?
faqs.a: Both are possible project directions, but they need different infrastructure. The channel and its feasibility are confirmed in the proposal; voice coverage is not assumed.

faqs.q: Can it confirm appointments?
faqs.a: Only when the agreed system can reliably check availability and create a booking. Otherwise it collects a request for a person to confirm.

faqs.q: What happens when it cannot help?
faqs.a: The design should provide a human route and retain the relevant enquiry context, with a fallback if the receiving team is unavailable.

name: Restaurant WhatsApp automation
title: Restaurant WhatsApp Enquiry and Order Automation
description: Plan restaurant WhatsApp automation with Hamid for menu enquiries, structured order requests and staff confirmation, with clear availability and delivery checks.
intro: Restaurant WhatsApp automation can help guests find menu information and submit structured order requests. A useful system checks what it knows, gathers the details staff need and distinguishes an order request from an accepted order.
problem: Free-form order messages can omit quantities, addresses or collection times. Menus also change. Automation must use an owned, up-to-date source and keep unavailable items or delivery exceptions visible to staff.
audience: Restaurants, cafés and delivery teams receiving WhatsApp menu and ordering enquiries. It suits a team willing to maintain menu data and define who confirms requests.
features: Menu questions using approved item and price data
Structured collection of items, quantities and contact details
Delivery or collection requests with explicit confirmation status
Staff notifications and a human path for special requests
flow: Review the menu source, ordering process and fulfilment responsibilities.
Confirm WhatsApp platform access and any ordering-system integration.
Design the cart, request summary and staff approval steps.
Test unavailable items, address changes and duplicate submissions.
example: A guest could ask about a dish, choose quantities and receive a request summary. Staff then confirm availability and fulfilment. Payment collection, live stock and automatic acceptance are separate features that require reliable integrations.
integration: A maintained spreadsheet may suit a small menu, while a POS or ordering API may support a more connected workflow. Compatibility and access are checked rather than assumed. Provider charges are separate from development scope.

faqs.q: Can it take restaurant orders?
faqs.a: It can be designed to collect order requests. Automatic acceptance requires verified availability, pricing and fulfilment logic; staff approval is a practical starting point.

faqs.q: Will it know when an item sells out?
faqs.a: Only if availability is maintained in its approved source or a connected system. Otherwise staff confirmation is needed.

faqs.q: Can delivery fees be calculated?
faqs.a: An agreed rule or supported delivery integration is needed. Ambiguous addresses and exceptions should be reviewed by staff.

name: Website chatbot
title: Website Chatbot Development for Helpful Enquiries
description: Add a helpful website chatbot with Hamid for approved FAQs, enquiry capture and human handover. Plan its content, accessibility and integrations around visitors.
intro: A website chatbot gives visitors a conversational route to information and your team. I can plan a chatbot around approved FAQs, relevant pages and structured enquiry capture, while keeping the website usable without opening the chat.
problem: Visitors may not know which service page answers their question. A chatbot can guide them, but it should not invent an answer, block navigation or replace clear website content. The business needs ownership of the answers and an escalation path.
audience: Businesses with repeated website questions, complex service choices or a useful lead qualification step. Existing sites can be assessed without assuming they need a full rebuild.
features: Answers grounded in approved website or knowledge content
Links to the relevant service and contact pages
Optional lead details with clear field labels
Accessible controls, mobile layout and a human contact route
flow: Review the existing site, common questions and content gaps.
Choose the knowledge source and define what the assistant may answer.
Build a lightweight interface and optional lead connection.
Test keyboard use, narrow screens, wrong questions and failures.
example: A visitor deciding between a landing page and a business website could receive a short explanation and links to both services. If they need a custom quote, the assistant can collect a brief or direct them to you rather than guessing a price.
integration: Embedding depends on the current website and hosting access. Optional email, CRM or spreadsheet connections need suitable permissions. Third-party scripts are assessed for their loading cost and data handling.

faqs.q: Can a chatbot work with my existing website?
faqs.a: Often, if the site permits an embed or code change. The platform, hosting restrictions and required integrations are checked first.

faqs.q: Does it replace my contact page?
faqs.a: No. Visitors should still have direct contact options and readable service information, including when chat is unavailable.

faqs.q: How does it avoid made-up answers?
faqs.a: Use an approved knowledge source, test likely questions and define a fallback for unsupported topics. Review and maintenance remain necessary.

name: AI agents
title: Custom AI Agent Development with Clear Boundaries
description: Scope an AI agent with Hamid for a defined business task. Agree on tool access, human approvals, evaluation examples and monitoring before allowing actions.
intro: An AI agent can choose steps and use tools within an assigned task, rather than following only a fixed sequence. I help define where that flexibility is useful and where predictable workflows or human decisions are a better fit.
problem: Giving a model access to tools without clear permissions can create confusing or incorrect actions. A useful agent starts with a narrow objective, approved information, bounded tool access and a measurable definition of completion.
audience: Teams with tasks that vary enough to need decisions about the next step, and who can provide examples and review outputs. A simple rules-based process may be more suitable for repetitive, predictable work.
features: A defined task with explicit permitted actions
Read-only access before consequential tool use where practical
Human approval for important changes or communications
Evaluation cases, activity logs and a stopping condition
flow: Compare the task against a simpler workflow alternative.
Define the tools, permissions and acceptable outcomes.
Prototype against representative and difficult examples.
Review reliability and operating cost before expanding access.
example: An internal assistant might retrieve approved information, prepare a summary and propose a next step. Sending messages, altering records or making financial commitments would require separately agreed controls. This is an illustrative design, not a claimed client deployment.
integration: AI APIs and business tools are chosen after confirming their capabilities and credentials. Secrets stay outside public website code. Evaluation and usage costs form part of the project discussion.

faqs.q: How is an agent different from a chatbot?
faqs.a: A chatbot is a conversational interface. An agent additionally decides how to use available tools to pursue a task; not every chatbot needs that behaviour.

faqs.q: Should an agent run without approval?
faqs.a: That depends on the consequences. Start with narrow access and require a person to approve consequential actions until the controls and reliability are established.

faqs.q: What should I bring to discovery?
faqs.a: A description of the task, examples of successful outcomes, the tools involved and the actions that must remain under human control.

descriptor: AI agent development with defined controls

name: Workflow automation
title: Workflow Automation for Forms, Leads and Operations
description: Connect routine business steps with Hamid: forms, lead routing, follow-ups and operational updates, with duplicate checks, retries and clear ownership.
intro: Workflow automation connects a trigger to a defined series of actions: a form arrives, information is checked and the right person is notified. I help turn a repeated business process into a maintainable flow with clear exception handling.
problem: Moving the same information between a form, spreadsheet and inbox takes attention away from customers. Automating the happy path alone is not enough: duplicate submissions, missing fields and unavailable tools also need a plan.
audience: Agencies and businesses managing enquiries, assignments, status updates or regular operational tasks. The process should have a named owner who can decide how exceptions are handled.
features: Triggers from supported forms, schedules or webhooks
Field validation and duplicate detection
Routing and updates between approved tools
Failure notifications, retry rules and an activity trail
flow: Draw the current process and remove unnecessary steps.
Choose the trigger, required fields and receiving tools.
Build and test normal, duplicate and failed executions.
Hand over the workflow with an owner and maintenance notes.
example: A new enquiry can create a record, notify the assigned person and prepare a follow-up task. If a receiving tool is unavailable, the process should retain the request and flag it rather than silently losing the lead.
integration: Make, webhooks and supported APIs can be considered according to the task. Google Sheets or a CRM may be a useful destination when access is available. AI is optional and should serve a specific step.

faqs.q: Can workflows connect with Google Sheets?
faqs.a: That can be included when the account and integration provide suitable access. Sheet structure, permissions and duplicate handling are agreed first.

faqs.q: What happens if an integration fails?
faqs.a: The design should include appropriate retries, a visible error notification and a way to recover the affected request.

faqs.q: Is ongoing maintenance needed?
faqs.a: Yes. Provider changes, expired access and changes to your process can affect a workflow. Ownership and support scope are agreed before handover.

name: Web development
title: Web Development in Pakistan for Businesses — Hamid
description: Work directly with Hamid on a business website with clear content, responsive design and useful enquiries. Explore real portfolio sites and discuss your scope.
intro: I build business websites that explain what you offer and give visitors a clear next step. Projects bring content, visual direction and practical functionality together, with attention to mobile screens and the everyday work behind the site.
problem: A good-looking homepage is only part of the job. Visitors also need to understand the service, trust the information and find a way to enquire. The site needs an agreed content structure, reliable contact paths and a plan for updates after launch.
audience: Independent businesses, creative professionals and agencies looking for a technical partner. I work from Pakistan with remote clients; project discussions can include businesses in Islamabad, Rawalpindi and other markets without requiring an office visit.
features: A page structure built around your actual offer
Responsive layouts with practical mobile navigation
Portfolio, collection or service content as appropriate
Enquiry paths, page metadata and launch checks
flow: Agree on the audience, page list, content and project scope.
Develop a visual direction and representative page layouts.
Build the site and connect the agreed forms or contact routes.
Review accessibility, mobile use and deployment before handover.
example: The portfolio includes bridal, jewellery, photography, creative and service websites. Open their live demos and desktop/mobile previews to assess the visual direction and enquiry journeys. Detailed overviews cover visible features without claiming unverified conversion results.
integration: The framework and hosting are selected for the site's needs. This portfolio uses Next.js and static rendering; a client project may require a different setup. Payments, ecommerce and editable content are scoped separately when needed.

faqs.q: How much does a business website cost?
faqs.a: The page count, content, visual complexity, editing needs and integrations determine the quote. Share an outline or references for a scoped proposal rather than a guessed price.

faqs.q: How long does development take?
faqs.a: A schedule follows discovery and depends on content readiness, functionality and review rounds. A fixed delivery promise is not made before the scope is agreed.

faqs.q: Can you work with an agency?
faqs.a: Yes. I work directly with businesses and alongside agencies needing a technical partner. Responsibilities and communication are agreed for each project.

name: Landing page development
title: Landing Page Development for a Clear Next Step
description: Build a focused landing page with Hamid for your service or campaign: clear messaging, real proof, mobile-friendly layouts and a measurable enquiry path.
intro: A landing page presents one offer and guides visitors towards one main action. I help shape the message, supporting proof and page flow so a campaign visitor can understand the offer before deciding to enquire.
problem: Sending campaign traffic to a broad homepage can leave the next step unclear. A focused page needs a specific audience, a truthful promise and an appropriate call to action. Design supports that message; it cannot guarantee conversions on its own.
audience: Businesses launching a service, promoting a campaign or collecting qualified enquiries. It is useful when the traffic source and desired visitor action are known.
features: An offer-led introduction and clear primary action
Real screenshots, examples or approved testimonials
A readable mobile page with well-spaced tap targets
Form or WhatsApp enquiry routes and optional measurement setup
flow: Define the campaign audience, traffic source and action.
Organise the offer, objections and available proof.
Design and build the page around a straightforward journey.
Check the enquiry path and measurement before sending traffic.
example: A service campaign page could explain who the offer suits, show relevant work and answer the questions that hold visitors back. Its form should ask only what your team needs for a useful first response.
integration: Forms, booking links, WhatsApp and analytics can be considered depending on the campaign. Tracking IDs and destination accounts must belong to the business; no placeholder analytics is enabled on a live page.

faqs.q: Do I need a landing page or a full website?
faqs.a: A landing page suits one focused offer. A full website is usually more useful when visitors need to explore several services, projects and business information.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee a conversion rate?
faqs.a: No. Offer quality, traffic, pricing and follow-up all affect outcomes. Clear messaging and measurement make informed improvements possible.

faqs.q: Can it use my existing branding?
faqs.a: Yes. Share brand files, approved content and examples. A focused page can extend your existing visual identity.

name: Business dashboards
title: Custom Business Dashboards for Clear Operations
description: Plan a business dashboard with Hamid for enquiries, status and operational data, with agreed metrics, role-based access and clear ownership of each source.
intro: A business dashboard brings relevant information into one place so a team can see what needs attention. I can scope a custom interface around your operating questions, data sources and the actions each person is allowed to take.
problem: A dashboard cannot fix conflicting or incomplete records by itself. Useful reporting begins with shared definitions: what counts as a lead, who owns it and when its status changes. Data freshness and access need to be visible rather than assumed.
audience: Teams tracking enquiries, tasks, orders or operational status across several tools. It is best scoped around the decisions a team makes each day, rather than a collection of decorative charts.
features: An agreed set of metrics and status views
Search and filters appropriate to the team's workflow
Access controls defined for each role
Clear source, update time and unavailable-data states
flow: Identify the decisions the dashboard should support.
Audit available data sources and agree on metric definitions.
Prototype the views and permissions with representative records.
Test accuracy, access boundaries and updates before use.
example: An enquiry dashboard might show new requests, assigned owners and follow-ups due. A useful first version can focus on this queue before adding charts or automated actions. This is a possible scope, not an existing client result.
integration: Spreadsheets, databases and supported business APIs may provide the data. Private dashboards require a separate application with appropriate authentication and server-side credentials; they should not be exposed as public marketing pages.

faqs.q: Can it show data from multiple tools?
faqs.a: Potentially, if each source provides suitable access and records can be matched reliably. Data definitions and update frequency need to be agreed first.

faqs.q: Will the data update in real time?
faqs.a: That depends on source capabilities and the required operating cost. The proposal should state the actual refresh behaviour rather than promise real-time updates by default.

faqs.q: Who can access the dashboard?
faqs.a: Access is scoped by role and verified through authentication. Public website visitors should not have access to private operational records.

name: Growth Engine
descriptor: Search & AI visibility, including SEO, AEO and GEO
title: SEO, AEO & GEO Services | Growth Engine — Hamid
description: Technical SEO, answer-focused content, AI search readiness and clearer conversion paths. Explore Growth Engine, a developer-led visibility service by Hamid.
headline: Get found.
Get understood.
Give people a reason to choose you.
intro: I help businesses strengthen their websites for Google Search, useful AI-powered answers and the real decisions visitors make before getting in touch.
problem: Good design makes an impression. People still need to discover your pages, understand your offer and find an easy next step. When those connections are missing, even a carefully built website can struggle to generate meaningful enquiries.

deliverables.title: Search foundations
deliverables.detail: Make important pages easier for search engines to access, understand and index.
deliverables.checks: Crawl and indexation checks, canonical URLs, sitemaps, robots directives, titles, internal links, mobile performance and relevant structured data.
deliverables.sample: Prioritized technical findings with affected URLs, a proposed fix and the check used to verify it.

deliverables.title: Answer readiness
deliverables.detail: Give people direct, accurate answers to the questions that matter before they enquire.
deliverables.checks: Buyer questions, search intent, answer-first sections, examples, attributable sources, clear authorship and contextual links.
deliverables.sample: A buyer-question map that pairs each question with a page update and the evidence it needs.

deliverables.title: AI discovery
deliverables.detail: Improve the clarity, access and supporting evidence that AI-powered search can draw on when describing your business.
deliverables.checks: Crawlable HTML, bot access, consistent business and service details, sourceable explanations and dated observations where useful.
deliverables.sample: An AI search-readiness checklist and an observation log with dates, queries and limitations.

deliverables.title: Conversion paths
deliverables.detail: Make the next step clear when the right visitor arrives.
deliverables.checks: Page hierarchy, contact copy, mobile tap targets, form feedback and working paths to an enquiry. Track contact actions with consent.
deliverables.sample: A list of friction points, the agreed fixes and verified contact paths on desktop and mobile.

deliverables.title: Measurement and iteration
deliverables.detail: See what changed across discovery, site visits and meaningful enquiries.
deliverables.checks: Search Console and GA4 setup, a dated baseline, priority landing pages, contact events and AI referral or prompt observations where data is available.
deliverables.sample: A before-and-after change log, known data gaps and dates for reviewing the results.

fit.title: Growing business
fit.text: Your website is live, and you want the right visitors to understand the offer and take a clear next step.
fit.firstStep: Review the service page that matters most and follow its path to contact.

fit.title: Startup or founder
fit.text: You want to launch with clear pages, technical search foundations and a way to learn what visitors do.
fit.firstStep: Agree the priority pages and launch checks before the site goes live.

fit.title: Agency partner
fit.text: You need a developer who can translate technical recommendations into reliable client-site changes and clear handover notes.
fit.firstStep: Review your roadmap, access and the fixes that are ready to implement.

process.title: Diagnose
process.text: Understand your goals, priority pages, current visibility and what data is available.

process.title: Prioritize
process.text: Agree which technical, content or enquiry issues deserve attention first, and how to check each fix.

process.title: Implement
process.text: Ship the agreed improvements and verify them on real devices and published URLs.

process.title: Measure & refine
process.text: Review a dated baseline, record what changed and decide what to do next.

outputs.title: Visibility audit
outputs.detail: Affected pages, findings, reasons for prioritization and suggested fixes.

outputs.title: Page and content plan
outputs.detail: Search topics and buyer questions mapped to the pages that should answer them.

outputs.title: Implemented improvements
outputs.detail: Technical and on-page changes within scope, with links to the updated pages.

outputs.title: Conversion checks
outputs.detail: A walkthrough of the contact path and checks for the agreed fixes on real devices.

outputs.title: Measurement handover
outputs.detail: Setup notes, metric definitions, available baselines and documented data gaps.

limits: I agree the pages, deliverables and verification with you before the work starts. Content production, third-party mentions, analytics access and ongoing monitoring depend on the scope and access. Search and AI platforms decide what to index, rank, cite or recommend.

faqs.q: What’s the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO?
faqs.a: Search engine optimization (SEO) improves how people find relevant pages in search. Answer engine optimization (AEO) makes useful answers easier to retrieve and understand. Generative engine optimization (GEO) addresses how AI search can discover, understand and reference your business.

faqs.q: Can you guarantee the first page of Google or recommendations in ChatGPT?
faqs.a: Google and AI platforms decide which pages to rank, cite or recommend. I can improve technical access, content clarity, evidence and measurement. Exposure varies by platform, query and context.

faqs.q: Does my website need a complete redesign?
faqs.a: An existing site is usually a good place to start. I review access, page structure and enquiry routes first. A redesign makes sense when the existing implementation limits the goal.

faqs.q: What if my website has very little Search Console data?
faqs.a: I can still check crawl access, indexing signals, internal links and contact paths. I record the starting evidence and track changes when enough data is available.

faqs.q: How long will changes take to show results?
faqs.a: I can verify the agreed technical fixes once they go live. Changes in indexing, traffic or enquiries depend on the starting point, competition and search platform. I agree practical dates to review the evidence.

faqs.q: Do I need a special llms.txt file or an AI-only schema?
faqs.a: Google’s AI features use the ordinary Search requirements and eligible pages. I start with crawlable pages, useful content, appropriate structured data and genuine evidence. Other platforms publish their own discovery controls.

faqs.q: Can you work directly with my developer or agency?
faqs.a: Yes. I agree ownership, access, page scope, responsibilities and handover before implementing changes.

faqs.q: What will you measure?
faqs.a: Where I have access, I check indexing, relevant search visits, contact clicks and qualified enquiries. A click records interest. Confirmed enquiries come from conversations your team actually receives. Dated AI referrals and prompt observations can add context.
